text:
alex: quick heads-up — after the kernel-prioritizer V2 roll we’re seeing a 12-18% throughput regression on the h100 mixed-packing fleet. perf traces point to increased KV-cache fragmentation + a lot more kernel fallbacks to the scalar path.

maria: ack. seen similar in the a100 subset too, though less severe (5-7%). any sample traces? :eyes: 

alex: pasted a short profiler dump from a representative request (h100). TL;DR: avg tokens-per-batch went up (420 -> 560) and KV hit-rate dropped ~9%.

```
# profiler snippet: h100 run 2026-03-18T10:23Z
batch_count: 1387
avg_tokens_batch: 560
avg_latency_ms: 82.4
kv_cache_hits: 0.81  # pre-roll ~0.90
kernel_path_breakdown: optimized=58%, fallback_scalar=42%
memory_frag_pct: 12.3
```

ben: that's interesting — fallback_scalar at 42% is huge. kernel selector change must be misclassifying some sequences as kernel-incompatible (maybe due to KV fragment thresholds).

katie: what do we mean by "KV fragmentation" here? is it eviction churn or layout misalignment?

alex: looks like layout misalignment + more small-slice batches causing KV pages to be underutilized. profiler shows a lot of small LRU churn windows right after the selector picks a kernel variant.

maria: hypothesis: the prioritizer now prefers higher packing to improve throughput, so batches contain more heterogeneous seq lengths. That increases prefix diversity -> KV cache locality suffers -> kernel fallback because some kernels require contiguous KV shapes.

ben: actionable: temporarily tighten max_tokens_per_batch on H100/A100 to force smaller, more homogeneous batches so KV locality recovers while we iterate on selector heuristics. Suggested soft caps: H100=480, A100=400, A10=360, L4=320, T4=240.

alex: can we run a 2h canary with those caps on a fraction of traffic? If we see kv-hit ~0.88+ and fallbacks <25% we know caps help.

devops-bot: deploy plan queued by katie: rollout 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 10m watch windows. rollback on 3xx latency regressions or error spike.

katie: scheduling canary now. will start with h100 pool only, 5% traffic. I'll attach dashboard link once live.

maria: parallel work: i'll add logging to kernel-prioritizer to emit the exact reason for kernel pick (kernel_id + mismatch_flags) and a compact histogram of seq_length variance per batch. we need data to see whether selector thresholds are the root cause.

ben: also enabling a perf counter to measure "kv-contiguity-score" (rough metric: fraction of requests in a batch that share a common KV page). should help quantify locality.

alex: a couple of notes from profiling to consider for longer-term fixes:
- adapt kernel selection to be KV-aware: prefer kernels that tolerate fragmentation when contiguity-score low.
- add a packer option: prefer homogeneity over raw packing when contiguity below threshold.
- consider a micro-rebalance that splits a large heterogeneous batch into two packing-similar sub-batches before kernel selection.

katie: can we get a quick perf test harness run to simulate the micro-rebalance idea? small synthetic workload with zipf-ish length distribution would be ideal.

ben: yep — I can run a 30min harness across all card types with proto-split. will capture latency tail, avg tokens/batch, kv-hit, and fallback%.

alex: post-canary checklist: if the soft caps restore perf, we will
- keep caps as temporary mitigations
- ship selector logging + contiguity counters
- iterate kernel-prioritizer rules (maria + ben)
- evaluate micro-rebalance in harness (ben)

maria: I’ll create a short RFC for KV-aware kernel selection and include perf expectations. target: ship alpha heuristics in 2 sprints.

devops-bot: canary started: 5% to h100 pool. watch dashboard: https://dashboard.internal/r/kv-frag-canary-3745678912

katie: initial 10m: latency down 6% vs post-roll baseline, kv-hit improved to 0.87 (from 0.81), fallback_scalar now 29%. promising. continuing to 20% in 30m.

alex: great. @maria @ben assignable items?

maria: i'll own selector logging + RFC.

ben: i'll own perf harness micro-rebalance tests and contiguity metric instrument.

katie: I'll run the staged rollout and capture dashboards + smoke tests.

alex: thanks. we'll regroup after 2h canary and decide whether to expand caps to A100/A10.

perf-bot: perf alert suppressed for rollout window. will resume normal alerts at end of canary.

katie: quick note — let's include a postmortem if caps stay >24h. we should document root cause and long-term plan in eng-runtime.

alex: agreed. logging and metrics first. thanks all. :heart:
